priority_definitions.P0: Blocks the 'genuinely production-grade, highest-fidelity map' claim outright. A default-path defect that materially misrepresents the map's structure or is invisible to existing gates.
priority_definitions.P1: Significant, real gap. Should be fixed before a production_candidate acceptance profile can be trusted, but does not misrepresent what's already measured.
priority_definitions.P2: Real gap, lower urgency. Either narrow-impact, already mitigated by an off-by-default flag, or a documentation/consistency issue with a defect underneath.
priority_definitions.P3: Documentation/consistency only, or a properly-gated, low-risk hardcode.

gaps.title: Lane count is never derived from OSM -- every road always gets exactly 1 driving lane per side
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/lane_generator.py::LaneGenerator.ensure_lanes (lines 104-188) unconditionally creates exactly one left id=1 and one right id=-1 driving lane per non-junction road (one right lane for connectors). OSM lanes=/lanes:forward/lanes:backward tags ARE parsed by lane_width_policy.py::_lane_count_from_meta, but that count is used ONLY as a divisor for the osm_width_per_lane width tier -- never to determine how many <lane> elements to emit. No multi-lane generation logic exists anywhere in lane_generator.py.
gaps.impact: A genuinely 4-lane arterial road and a 1-lane service road receive structurally identical lane topology in the output. This directly contradicts the stated goal of 'highest-fidelity map supported by the available OSM... inputs' -- the single largest, most consequential structural fidelity gap found in this audit.

gaps.title: 20.3% of junction-connector road-boundary links have a geometric offset of exactly one lane-width, invisible to the acceptance gate
gaps.evidence: Fresh measurement against the pinned map-of-record via check_geometric_continuity.py: 9,176 of 45,178 junction-connector links (20.3%) exceed eps_xy=0.05m. Median offset is EXACTLY 3.5m (this generator's standard lane width); max values cluster at exact multiples of 3.5m (14.0m=4x, 10.5m=3x, 7.0m=2x). check_geometric_continuity.py deliberately routes junction-connector links to a separate, non-gating bucket by design -- so this large, systematic signal never affects `ok`/`valid_for_experiments`.
gaps.impact: Strongly suggests connector reference-lines are anchored to the wrong lane-boundary/lane-index rather than the road centerline in roughly 1 in 5 junction connections -- a structural correctness issue currently completely undetected by the acceptance pipeline. Regression-test corpus (10 worst by offset): roads 69981, 69984, 69987 (14.0m each), 68258, 69384, 69597, 69111, 69919, 69815, 69917 (10.5m each).

gaps.title: 27 isolated lane components, root-caused as a systematic LANELINK_DEFECT
gaps.evidence: component_reachability_summary confirms 27 isolated lane-level components (26 unique roads) on the current pin. Full XML chain-walk of all 26: every isolated lane is the road's OUTERMOST driving lane; the downstream junction connection's laneLink set always covers from=-1 through from=-(n-1) but never from=-n. The connectingRoad and downstream road both consistently have exactly N-1 driving lanes (one fewer than the incoming road). One road (51767, Gustave-Trouve-Strasse) is more severe -- never wired into any junction connection at all.
gaps.impact: Independently re-derives and CONFIRMS a prior investigation's conclusion (see project_round4_junction_connection_coverage_20260904 memory): this is zero valid connector candidates, not a disambiguation problem -- fixing requires synthesizing new connector geometry/lane content that doesn't exist in the source pipeline output. Root cause is upstream of the connector layer: the junction-connector generation stage builds the connecting-road chain with the wrong lane count relative to the incoming road.
gaps.impact_note: This is a KNOWN, previously-scoped gap, not newly discovered -- included here so the gap register is complete and the LANELINK_DEFECT classification (refined from the prior generic 'generator defect' label) is on record.

gaps.title: ConnectorValidator explicitly skips lane-section and attachment-pose validation
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/topology/junction_connector_rebuild.py, ConnectorValidator.validate() (lines 22-35): lane-section and attachment-pose checks are present in the source as COMMENTED-OUT lines with '# E1.5: validate lane sections (SKIP for now)' and '# E1.8: validate attachment poses (SKIP for now)'. Only planView existence and non-negative length are actually checked.
gaps.impact: The validator's own author documented this gap in the code; it was never closed. Mitigated in practice by: (a) the connector-rebuild feature is off by default (UP_ENABLE_JUNCTION_CONNECTOR_REBUILD=0), (b) a separate JunctionIntegrityGate covers dangling refs/lane-link existence as an unconditional hard-fail gate. Rated P0 because it is the exact validator the audit brief specifically called out, and because when the rebuild feature IS used (any experimental/development run), zero pose/lane-section validation occurs.

gaps.title: Position-specific OSM metadata (turn:lanes, regulatory signs) propagated via street-name-only matching with no confidence/ambiguity handling
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/osm_meta_index.py builds a pure Dict[street_name, metadata] with no spatial component. turn_lanes_writer.py::apply_turn_lanes and regulatory_sign_writer.py::apply_regulatory_signs (both called unconditionally from stage_04_enrichment.py's live pipeline path whenever osm_meta is non-empty) stamp the looked-up value onto EVERY XODR road sharing that street name. Both modules' own docstrings self-document the risk: a value scoped to one intersection approach in OSM 'may be applied to every XODR road segment sharing that name.' No confidence scoring or ambiguous-match rejection exists -- a single dict lookup always silently applies if found.
gaps.impact: One street name commonly maps to many distinct XODR segments after the OSM->XODR conversion splits at intersections. A turn-lane hint or regulatory sign scoped to one approach can be silently mis-applied to unrelated segments of the same-named street. Real risk, confirmed reachable in the live pipeline, not just an offline/analysis-tool concern.
gaps.positive_counter_example: ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/crosswalk_writer.py implements genuine geometric correspondence (real footway=crossing node geometry, curve-aware nearest-point matching, 5m threshold, spatial grid index) -- proof the team already knows how to do this correctly; it simply wasn't applied to turn-lanes/signs.

gaps.title: Duplicate SemanticOverlapChecker classes: the live-wired one is a non-geometric heuristic; the real polygon-intersection implementation is dead code
gaps.evidence: Two different classes share the name SemanticOverlapChecker. (1) ultimate_pipeline/quality/check_semantic_overlap.py::validate() -- wired live via quality_gate_manager.py::gate_semantic_overlap -- only flags a road if it has BOTH a sidewalk-type AND building-type object attached to the SAME road element; no coordinates, no polygons, no actual geometric intersection test, and its own docstring calls itself 'intentionally lightweight.' (2) ultimate_pipeline/quality/semantic_overlap.py::check() -- a genuine Shapely polygon-intersection implementation -- confirmed via repo-wide grep to be imported NOWHERE except a stale submission-mirror file listing; never actually executed.
gaps.impact: The map's only wired 'semantic overlap' gate cannot detect an actual building-overlaps-road defect -- it can only detect co-attachment to the same road element, which is a much weaker and largely unrelated signal. A real, working implementation already exists in the codebase and is simply not connected to anything.
gaps.mitigating_context: map_acceptance.py's own comments confirm both semantic_overlap and collision_mesh are deliberately soft/non-fatal by design (never appear in hard_fail_reasons) -- so this gap does not currently block promotion, but it does mean the map's semantic-overlap posture is effectively unmeasured.

gaps.title: No second-city (or any) fixture exists -- every structural algorithm is validated on Ingolstadt only
gaps.evidence: Exhaustive search found no campaigns/*munich* or equivalent second-city directory anywhere in the repo. ultimate_pipeline/analysis/cross_city.py's Munich references are purely illustrative docstring examples of a naming convention, never backed by real data. ultimate_pipeline/hpc/hpc_training_launcher.py's multi-city config stubs are speculative and not wired into main_pipeline.py or cli.py (zero call sites).
gaps.impact: Confirms the audit brief's suspicion directly: no structural algorithm in this pipeline (junction rebuild, roundabout reconstruction, elevation policy, lane generation) has ever been validated against a second real city. RQ2/RQ3/RQ5-style generalization claims have zero supporting evidence beyond Ingolstadt. This is an evidence gap, not a code defect, but it blocks any 'production-grade, generalizes beyond one city' claim.
gaps.note: Requires acquiring a second city's OSM+DEM data -- an operator/data-acquisition task, not a Codex code task.

gaps.title: Roundabout reconstruction collapses multi-lane roundabouts to single-lane and forces a perfect circle
gaps.evidence: See docs/map_quality/JUNCTIONS_AND_ROUNDABOUTS.md for full detail. Quantified against real data: 20 of 81 lane-tagged OSM roundabouts in the pinned source (25%) are multi-lane; all would be collapsed if reconstruction ran.
gaps.impact: Bounded severity: ENABLE_ROUNDABOUT_RECONSTRUCTION defaults False in every named release profile, so the live/production map's roundabout geometry currently passes through from the upstream converter largely unmodified by this codebase. Rated P1 (not P0) because the defect is real but not currently exercised by the production path.

gaps.title: Bridge/tunnel elevation ('deck_linear' policy) has no independent deck-height/clearance data source
gaps.evidence: structure_classifier.py correctly spatially classifies bridge/tunnel/underpass roads from OSM tags and maps them to a 'deck_linear' policy (verified live, matches commit e3f91dbc). But apply_dem (elevation_importer.py:793-924) still samples the SAME ground-terrain Copernicus GLO-30 GeoTIFF at the road's two endpoints for a 'deck_linear' road -- there is no bridge-height/deck-height/clearance data source anywhere in the module (confirmed via exhaustive grep).
gaps.impact: For a bridge whose two endpoints are correctly ground-sampled (e.g. valley-wall abutments), linear interpolation between them produces a reasonable deck profile by construction. The real residual risk is any bridge whose endpoint samples themselves land on a CRS/offset mismatch, nodata, or a raster cell contaminated by nearby structures -- nothing validates that an endpoint sample represents 'top of abutment' rather than 'ground beneath the abutment.' No deck-vs-ground separation is ever checked.

gaps.title: No minimum bridge-deck-to-ground separation or tunnel-specific elevation threshold exists
gaps.evidence: Exhaustive threshold sweep across settings.py and stage_05_geometry.py found explicit, enforced numeric thresholds for max grade, elevation smoothness, elevation continuity, elevation seams, and DEM coverage/quality -- but NONE for minimum bridge-deck-to-ground separation, and NONE specific to tunnels (tunnels get the identical 2-point linear-interpolation treatment as bridges, with no check that a tunnel's elevation is actually below surrounding terrain).
gaps.impact: A structurally-classified bridge or tunnel could pass every existing elevation gate while having an implausible or physically-inconsistent deck/floor elevation relative to the terrain it's supposed to span or pass under.

gaps.title: Junction lane-link matching is index/sign-based, not geometry/heading-aware
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/lanes/lanelink_builder.py::LaneLinkBuilder.regenerate_lane_links pairs lanes purely by sign and |id| ordering (positive-to-positive, negative-to-negative, inner-first) via match_by_direction. Not geometry- or heading-aware.
gaps.impact: Can mispair lanes at complex junctions where lane cardinalities/orderings on each side don't correspond directionally in the naive index-sorted sense. sanitize_junction_lane_links, the module's own validation entrypoint, is a confirmed explicit stub (returns a hardcoded ok status with no real logic) -- so this mispairing risk has no independent safety net.

gaps.title: check_junction_connection_coverage.py -- a real, well-built diagnostic -- is not wired into any gate or pipeline stage
gaps.evidence: Confirmed via repo-wide import search: this module is imported nowhere else in the codebase. It implements genuine geometry+heading-aware CONFIDENT/AMBIGUOUS/NO_CANDIDATE classification for junction-connection coverage gaps, explicitly documented as read-only, but never called from run_gates() or any stage.
gaps.impact: A working detector for a real defect class sits unused. Low implementation cost to wire in (it already exists and is tested) relative to the value of the signal it produces.

gaps.title: Visual/collision QA (Phase J: OSM2World/Blender/FBX/collision/detached-slab) is real and tested but not wired into main_pipeline.py at all, and only validated at smoke-test scale
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/tools/phase_j_osm2world_blender.py (J1-J8) is substantive, real code with genuine execution evidence in reports/post_audit_hardening/{20260804T125500Z,20260804T130959Z,20260804T185517Z}/PHASE_J_OSM2WORLD_BLENDER.json (verdict J1_PASS/J4_OK/J5_ALIGNED/J6_PASS/J7_PASS/J8_PASS). But main_pipeline.py imports OSM2WorldRunner/is_osm2world_enabled and NEVER calls them in the pipeline body (zero call sites beyond the import). The validated scene in the real run evidence is tiny -- 19 vertices, 17 faces, 3 objects (2 placeholder + 1 ground plane) -- a smoke-test-scale artifact, not a full-map-scale validation.
gaps.impact: A real, working mesh-QA capability exists but has never been exercised against the actual ~149MB map-of-record. 'VISUAL_AND_COOKED_MAP_CERTIFICATE' (see PRODUCTION_MAP_QUALITY_CONTRACT.yaml) cannot currently be issued with any confidence at production scale.

gaps.title: No completeness metric comparing OSM source object counts to generated semantic object counts
gaps.evidence: map_acceptance.py::_enrichment_completeness_counts only checks generated counts are non-zero (fails only if functional_signals_count<=0 AND traffic_light_object_count<=0). No comparison against how many traffic_signals/crossing/etc tags exist in the source OSM for the same area. Exhaustive grep for such a comparison pattern returned zero hits anywhere in the codebase.
gaps.impact: The pipeline cannot currently answer 'did we generate roughly the number of traffic lights/signs/crosswalks the source data implies we should have' -- only 'did we generate at least one.'

gaps.title: Road-level graph-islands claim ('~9-10 components/~30 roads') does not reproduce against the current pinned map
gaps.evidence: Fresh run of structure_scanner.py::_analyze_graph_islands against the current pin: num_components=1, num_islands=0, covering all 32,267 roads -- a single connected component, at any threshold. The task brief's expected observation of ~9-10 components could not be reproduced.
gaps.impact: Unreconciled discrepancy, not silently resolved. Possible explanations (none confirmed): the ~9-10 number was measured against an earlier pin in the supersedes chain, or a different scanner invocation/threshold was used historically. No artifact was found recording exactly which prior pin produced that number.
gaps.note: This needs a human/provenance decision (which historical report is authoritative) rather than a code fix -- flagging for whoever owns the map-of-record history to reconcile or explicitly retire the old number.
gaps.resolution: RESOLVED (2026-09-07, by Claude, direct investigation, no code change needed): traced to reports/post_audit_hardening/C30_VISUAL_GEOMETRY_AUDIT/graph_components.json (component_count=10, largest_component_size=32267 -- the largest-component size matches the CURRENT map's total road count exactly, confirming this report's 'main' component is the same population, just with 9 additional small islands that no longer exist). C30's isolated_roads list (42367, 43405, 46369, 46698, 48129, 51654) matches exactly the '6 islands from C30' documented elsewhere in this repo's history as predating the stage_08_hygiene.py island-quarantine wiring fix (commit 1121e7c1, 2026-09-02) -- every governed regen since that fix correctly quarantines islands, so C30's report is accurate FOR ITS OWN (pre-fix) map generation and simply does not apply to the current, post-fix pin. Not a live regression; historical evidence correctly retired in favor of the current 1-component/0-islands measurement.

gaps.title: Global-injection software architecture pattern across all 13 pipeline-stage modules
gaps.evidence: Every one of the 13 files under ultimate_pipeline/pipeline_stages/ begins with an identical _inject_main_pipeline_globals() helper that copies the entire main_pipeline module namespace into the stage module's own globals at call time, and every stage function takes `self` (the live MainPipeline instance) and reads/writes its attributes directly with no declared contract. self.semantic_state is an untyped plain dict mutated by 4 different stages with no type enforcement.
gaps.impact: No compile-time or type-checked contract for what each stage actually requires or produces; harder to test stages in isolation; harder to reason about the real dependency graph (this audit's A1 agent had to read all 13 files' bodies to reconstruct it, since it isn't declared anywhere).
gaps.note: See A13 section of TARGET_PIPELINE_STAGE_GRAPH.md and PRODUCTION_MAP_TASK_GRAPH.json for the proposed incremental migration order (self.semantic_state first; stages 5/6/8 last).

gaps.title: Turn lanes are metadata-only -- never geometrically generated as dedicated lanes
gaps.evidence: turn_lanes_writer.py::apply_turn_lanes only writes a <userData><vector key="turnMarking"/></userData> hint from OSM turn:lanes; its own docstring explicitly states geometry is NOT modified. No code anywhere creates an additional dedicated left/right-turn <lane> element at an intersection approach (consistent with GAP-001's finding that lane count is never OSM-derived at all).
gaps.impact: Real dedicated turn lanes present in the source OSM data are never represented as actual drivable lane geometry in the output map -- only as a metadata hint a downstream consumer would have to interpret and act on themselves.

gaps.title: 180-degree tangent reversal on road 45622 -- a confirmed real, single-instance geometry defect on the current map-of-record
gaps.evidence: check_planview_internal_seams' heading-only bucket flags road 45622, geometry index 60->61, as a genuine 179.9999-degree tangent reversal. Independently verified by direct polynomial evaluation (not a checker artifact): the paramPoly3's own du/dp goes negative within its [0,1] domain -- the curve's own u-parametrization folds back on itself.
gaps.impact: A real authoring defect on the current pinned map-of-record, likely from an ill-conditioned curve fit during OSM geometry smoothing. This class of check is non-gating/diagnostic-only by design (82 heading-snap discontinuities total, of which this is the clear standout), so it does not currently block promotion, but a 180-degree reversal is a severe individual defect worth a dedicated regression fixture.
affected_files: road 45622 in the current map-of-record; upstream geometry-fitting code that produced it (not identified in this pass)

gaps.title: No lane-provenance metadata attached to the XODR output itself
gaps.evidence: LaneWidthDecision.source/.highway/.lane_count exist only as an in-memory dataclass and an aggregate JSON report (lane_width_policy_report.json); never attached to the XODR <lane>/<width> element (no userData vector, no attribute). Confirmed via a 116-hit grep for provenance/confidence/source patterns -- none attach a per-lane field to the element itself.
gaps.impact: A downstream consumer reading the XODR file alone cannot tell whether a given lane's width came from OSM, inference, or fallback -- must cross-reference a separate run-scoped JSON report that may not travel with the file.

gaps.title: No dedicated gate for unexplained lane-count changes
gaps.evidence: check_lane_section_successors.py repairs mismatched successor/predecessor lane-ID sets across laneSection boundaries but silently repairs links to whatever count exists -- it does not flag/report 'lane count changed here without explanation' as a quality metric.
gaps.impact: Real lane-count discontinuities (which could stem from GAP-001's single-lane-everywhere generation combined with any future multi-lane fix) would currently pass silently through repair rather than being surfaced for review.

gaps.title: No predecessor/successor consistency check or duplicate/conflicting-connection detection for junctions
gaps.evidence: Neither junction_connector_rebuild.py nor JunctionIntegrityGate implements a predecessor/successor consistency check or a duplicate-connection detector. The `processed_connectors` tracking in junction_connector_rebuild.py exists only to avoid double-processing within its own rebuild loop, not as a validation gate.
gaps.impact: Two connections that conflict (e.g. both claim the same lane pairing with contradictory contactPoints) would not be caught by any existing check.

gaps.title: structure_scanner.py's elevation-anomaly check is dead code on the current map
gaps.evidence: The check requires >=2 <elevation> records per road to compute any slope/jump metric (`if len(elevs) < 2: continue`), but every one of the 32,267 roads on the current pin has exactly 1 elevation record (this generator's single-polynomial-per-road encoding). It reports num_slope_segments=0 -- not because elevation is smooth, but because the check can never fire against this generator's output.
gaps.impact: A quality check that reports PASS but is structurally unable to catch a real defect class against this pipeline's own output format.

gaps.title: Curvature-anomaly check has a microsegment-inflation artifact
gaps.evidence: structure_scanner.py::_analyze_curvature uses a heading-delta/segment-length estimate. Verified: the top-ranked anomaly (road 51979, k=10.2) is driven by a real-but-small 0.148rad heading delta divided by a 1.4cm segment -- an approximation artifact of dividing by a near-zero length, not a genuinely sharp real-world turn. Confirmed 2 of the top 70 flagged roads share this artifact; the other 68 are genuine estimates on segments >=0.1m, still only an approximation (not true polynomial curvature) for paramPoly3/line segments lacking an explicit <arc>.
gaps.impact: A small fraction of the curvature-anomaly list is noise from the estimation method rather than real defects -- worth fixing before using this list to prioritize remediation work, otherwise effort gets misdirected at microsegment artifacts.

gaps.title: Heading-smoothing companion recompute guard (2026-09-04) has not been re-verified end-to-end
gaps.evidence: recompute_geometry_starts_chained_inplace's paramPoly3-boundary guard (commit 21cc6430, added after the C33 report documented 410 residual seams) has no follow-up C34/C35-style report re-running the full heading-smoothing scenario against it. The guard's own commit message frames it as 'defense-in-depth, not live-blocking' since the flag combination remains off by default.
gaps.impact: Unknown whether the guard actually resolves the 410-seam regression or merely prevents it from silently corrupting data (i.e., whether the scenario now cleanly completes, or now cleanly fails/skips more seams than before). Needs a dedicated experiment before ENABLE_UNSAFE_HEADING_ONLY_SMOOTHING + ENABLE_UNSAFE_GEOMETRY_START_RECOMPUTE could ever be safely relaxed.

gaps.title: No cycle-lane generation despite a dead width-table entry implying intent to support it
gaps.evidence: lane_generator.py's width table includes a 'cycleway' entry (2.0m) but no code path ever creates a type="biking" lane element -- the entry is dead for that purpose since only the single driving lane per side is ever generated.
gaps.impact: Minor relative to GAP-001/GAP-017, but a concrete example of the same underlying single-lane-generation limitation.

gaps.title: Roundabout reconstruction test-fixture gaps
gaps.evidence: See docs/map_quality/JUNCTIONS_AND_ROUNDABOUTS.md -- missing fixtures: multi-lane, elliptical, boundary-clipped, pedestrian-crossing, lane-count-change-partway-around roundabouts.
gaps.impact: Cannot regression-test fixes to GAP-008 without these fixtures existing first.

gaps.title: No z-fighting detection anywhere in the offline visual QA tooling
gaps.evidence: Zero hits anywhere in the codebase for 'z-fighting'/'z_fighting'. Phase J's other detached-slab/collision checks exist but this specific defect class has no detector.

gaps.title: check_junction_connection_coverage.py's comment inaccurately implies roundabout reconstruction is active
gaps.evidence: The module's comment says roundabout junctions are excluded from its analysis because they're 'wholesale-rewritten elsewhere' -- but reconstruction is confirmed off by default in every release profile (see GAP-008 context).

gaps.title: Two properly-gated, narrow Ingolstadt-specific hardcodes
gaps.evidence: (1) elevation_importer.py:1043, resolved_z=375.0 (Ingolstadt ground elevation), the last-resort tier of a 5-tier fallback chain, explicitly forbidden in the DEFAULT strict fallback-policy mode (only reachable via an explicit non-default lenient opt-in). (2) elevation_importer.py's _parse_utm_zone_from_georef falls back to zone 32 only when a geoReference string already contains utm/zone markers but the zone-number regex fails to match -- a near-unreachable degenerate-input edge case; the normal path correctly derives the zone from longitude.
gaps.impact: Both require an explicit non-default opt-in or a near-unreachable input condition to matter -- real but narrow/gated hazards, not silent default-path bugs. No `if city == "ingolstadt"`-style branches were found anywhere in core algorithm code.

gaps.title: .github/workflows/carla-runtime.yml has a fail-open evidence-integrity defect and cannot currently execute at all
gaps.evidence: Confirmed in the prior Stage-A runtime-admission audit this session (CODEX_RUNTIME_ADMISSION_EVIDENCE.json, written to session scratchpad, not the repo): the workflow's 'Write runtime health packet' step runs with `if: always()` and hardcodes `--test-result PASS --runtime-status PASS` unconditionally, regardless of whether the preceding live-CARLA verification step actually succeeded. Separately, zero self-hosted CI runners are registered for this repo (`gh api .../actions/runners` returns total_count=0), so the workflow cannot currently execute at all even if triggered.
gaps.impact: Not currently exploitable (the workflow has never run), but must be fixed before it is ever trusted -- as written, it can never report a live-CARLA failure even if one occurs. Included here so it has a durable, cross-referenceable home rather than living only in a prior session's scratchpad evidence file.
gaps.note: Also requires an OPERATOR action (registering a self-hosted runner) before it becomes exercisable at all -- the code fix alone is not sufficient.

gaps.title: Superelevation and crossfall are confirmed absent (documented omission, not a defect)
gaps.evidence: No code anywhere writes OpenDRIVE <superelevationProfile>/<superelevation> elements. Only 3 codebase hits for 'superelevation', all passive read-only detectors confirming absence, never generators. Crossfall/bank-angle: zero hits anywhere.
gaps.impact: Per the audit brief's own instruction ('do not fabricate superelevation purely for cosmetic improvement'), this is recorded as a documented, deliberate quality-dimension omission rather than a gap requiring immediate remediation -- included in the register for completeness and to make the omission explicit and trackable rather than silently absent.
gaps.note: A future decision point: is superelevation ever in scope for this project? If yes, this becomes a real P1/P2 task; if no, this entry should convert to an explicit WAIVED entry in the acceptance profile with a stated rationale.

gaps.title: roundabout_v2: internal API contradiction between core.validate_lane_mapping and lane_links.map_lanes/validate_links
gaps.source: Claude independent review of feature/roundabout-reconstruction-v2-20260907, verified directly by reading both functions and their tests
gaps.evidence: core.py::validate_lane_mapping unconditionally rejects any -1->-1 lane mapping as an invalid 'sentinel'. lane_links.py::map_lanes (the function actually used by the live ring-construction path, ring.py:100) correctly treats a real -1->-1 mapping as valid when both sides genuinely have a -1 lane. Both are exported in __init__.py.__all__ and both pass their own isolated unit tests, but they encode contradictory rules for the same conceptual check.
gaps.impact: A real misuse trap for whoever integrates this candidate further -- a future caller reaching for the more 'obvious'-sounding validate_lane_mapping instead of validate_links would incorrectly reject legitimate V2 output.

gaps.title: roundabout_v2: two undisclosed scope simplifications not listed in known_limitations
gaps.evidence: (1) ring.py:83 hardcodes 3.5m lane width for every generated ring segment instead of reusing lane_width_policy.py's OSM-derived width hierarchy. (2) ring.py:77 assumes zero grade at both anchor endpoints for the Hermite elevation fit instead of reading the source road's true grade at the anchor, which could introduce a small grade kink at the seam for non-flat roundabouts.
gaps.impact: Neither is a correctness bug; both are reasonable first-candidate scope choices, but neither is disclosed in the module's own known_limitations list, which only covers integration/CARLA/full-map-payload gaps.

gaps.title: roundabout_v2 evidence artifacts contain a verified-wrong test count
gaps.evidence: CODEX_ROUNDABOUT_V2_EVIDENCE.json claims "legacy_roundabout": "39 passed". Independently re-run on the exact same commit: tests/topology/test_roundabout_rebuilder.py (17 passed) + tests/topology/test_roundabout_reconstructor.py (27 passed) = 44 passed, 0 failed. Both files confirmed byte-identical to base via git diff. Separately, ROUNDABOUT_V2_BASELINE.json says "5825 collected" while the same evidence set elsewhere says "5830 collected" -- independently re-run: 5830 is correct.
gaps.impact: Under-claiming (reality is better than reported), not a hidden failure -- but a real, reproducible inaccuracy in self-reported evidence, meaning evidence JSON files from any agent should be spot-checked, not trusted verbatim.

gaps.title: GeometryValidator's missing-XY backfill formula is only correct for line primitives, applied unconditionally to all
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, independently spot-checked and CONFIRMED by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/geometry/geometry_validator.py:230 (verified directly): `dx = math.cos(h) * prev["length"]; dy = math.sin(h) * prev["length"]` runs for ANY previous geometry primitive with no check on prev's tag/type. This formula (straight-line displacement) is only geometrically correct if the previous geometry is a `line`. For `arc`, `spiral`, or `paramPoly3`, the true endpoint displacement is not `length * (cos(hdg), sin(hdg))`.
gaps.impact: When this backfill path fires (missing x/y attributes on a geometry element), it silently produces a wrong position for any road whose previous segment is curved -- exactly the kind of 'validator that is actually a repairer using unsafe approximations' pattern flagged in this session's broader architecture review.
gaps.note: This is one concrete instance of a broader pattern: multiple modules in this codebase (geometry_validator.py, structure_classifier.py's coarse sampler, older tiling bounds logic) each have their own partial/approximate geometry-primitive evaluators instead of sharing one canonical implementation. See GAP-037.

gaps.title: SidewalkBuilder has no explicit sidewalk=no branch -- falls through to default-both-sides
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, independently spot-checked and CONFIRMED by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/sidewalk_builder.py:175-187 (verified directly): the if/elif chain handles hint=='both'/'left'/'right' explicitly, then falls through to `elif default_both_sides:` for ANY other hint value including the explicit OSM `sidewalk=no` case -- there is no `elif hint == 'no': continue`/`pass` branch. Since `default_both_sides` defaults to True, a road explicitly tagged sidewalk=no in OSM still receives sidewalks added on both sides (unless it happens to be a motorway/trunk-class road).
gaps.impact: Directly contradicts explicit source truth -- the exact class of bug the audit brief calls out as most concerning: a fallback silently overriding an explicit, unambiguous OSM tag rather than a genuinely-missing one.

gaps.title: No single canonical OpenDRIVE geometry-primitive evaluator -- multiple partial/inconsistent implementations coexist
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document; partially corroborated by GAP-035 (a concrete instance) and by this session's own roundabout_v2 review (core.py's sample_road independently reimplements line/arc/paramPoly3/poly3 evaluation, a fourth implementation alongside geometry_validator.py, crosswalk_writer.py's curve-aware matcher, and structure_classifier.py's sampler)
gaps.evidence: Not independently re-verified line-by-line across every claimed site this session due to scope/time -- flagged here as a well-corroborated architectural finding (multiple genuinely independent geometry-evaluation code paths confirmed to exist: roundabout_v2/core.py::sample_road, geometry_validator.py, and per this session's earlier MQ-A audit, crosswalk_writer.py's curve-aware matcher) rather than a single-file bug. Codex should confirm the full extent (spiral/clothoid handling in particular) before treating this as fully scoped.
gaps.impact: Each consumer of OpenDRIVE geometry math (validation, crosswalk matching, structure classification, roundabout reconstruction, tiling bounds) can disagree about where a road actually is, especially for spiral/poly3 primitives which several of these implementations approximate as straight lines rather than evaluating exactly.
gaps.note: This is the single highest-leverage architectural fix available: unifying geometry evaluation into one canonical, tested module would retroactively fix GAP-035 and de-risk every downstream module that currently has its own partial implementation, including the roundabout_v2 candidate's own sampler.

gaps.title: Lane-width repair may flatten a genuine variable-width polynomial to a constant
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, not independently verified by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: Claimed: when lane_width_policy.py's repair path rewrites a width record, it writes a=target, b=0, c=0, d=0 unconditionally, which would replace a legitimate taper/merge/widening polynomial with a constant width regardless of whether the original polynomial was itself valid.
gaps.impact: If accurate, this would silently destroy real source-derived width variation (tapers, junction-approach widening) whenever the repair path fires for any reason, not just for genuinely invalid widths.
gaps.note: NEEDS INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION before being treated as confirmed -- included because it is concrete and falsifiable, not because it has been checked. First sub-task for whoever picks this up: confirm or refute against the actual code before implementing a fix.

gaps.title: Connectivity graph may use plain string road/junction IDs, risking collision between a road ID and a junction ID with the same value
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, not independently verified by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: Claimed: quarantine_island_roads()'s adjacency graph keys nodes by plain string ID without a type prefix, so a road and a junction that happen to share the same numeric ID string could collide in the same dictionary.
gaps.impact: If accurate, this could cause incorrect component/reachability analysis in edge cases where road and junction IDs overlap numerically.
gaps.note: NEEDS INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION before being treated as confirmed. Cheap to check (grep the graph-construction code for how node keys are built) and cheap to fix (prefix with 'road:'/'junction:') if real -- good candidate for a quick Codex confirm-then-fix pass.

gaps.title: Signal-to-lane validation checks lane-ID existence anywhere in the map, not scoped to the specific road/laneSection the signal claims to control
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, not independently verified by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: Claimed: validate_signal_references() collects lane IDs from the whole map globally and checks whether a referenced lane ID exists SOMEWHERE, rather than specifically on the road/laneSection at the signal's own s-position. Since lane IDs like -1/1 repeat on nearly every road, 'laneId=-1 exists somewhere' does not prove the signal controls a valid lane on its own intended road.
gaps.impact: If accurate, this validation could pass for a signal that references a real lane ID belonging to a completely unrelated road, giving false confidence that traffic-light/lane associations are correct.
gaps.note: NEEDS INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION before being treated as confirmed.

gaps.title: DEM elevation fallback policy's strict/lenient mode may be overridable by an environment variable even under a production release profile
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, not independently verified by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: Claimed: UP_ELEVATION_FALLBACK_POLICY=lenient can weaken the DEM fallback policy (which otherwise correctly forbids flat/extrapolated/hardcoded elevation) regardless of which RELEASE_PROFILE is active, i.e. an accidental or malicious environment variable could silently downgrade a production_candidate-profile run's elevation guarantees.
gaps.impact: If accurate, this is a governance gap in an otherwise well-designed safety mechanism (this session's own audit separately confirmed the strict-mode DEM fallback policy is one of the strongest safety designs in the repo) -- the release-profile system should be the sole authority over safety-critical fallback behavior, not overridable by a stray env var.
gaps.note: NEEDS INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION before being treated as confirmed. If real, the fix is narrow: release_profile.py should clamp/ignore this env var under any non-DEVELOPMENT/EXPERIMENTAL_UNSAFE profile, matching the pattern already used for the ENABLE_UNSAFE_* geometry flags (settings.py:372-402).

gaps.title: Tiling bounds cache may be keyed only by road ID, risking stale cross-map/cross-run results
gaps.source: Reported by an external analysis document, not independently verified by Claude this session
gaps.evidence: Claimed: a module-level _BOUNDS_CACHE in the tiler is keyed only by road ID, not scoped by map identity/run/geometry hash -- two different maps sharing a road ID (e.g. two regens of the same city, or a second-city fixture once GAP-007 is addressed) could read stale cached bounds from a previous map.
gaps.impact: If accurate, this could silently produce wrong tile boundaries when running the pipeline repeatedly in the same process (e.g. batch regeneration, or the eventual second-city regression corpus this audit program needs per GAP-007).
gaps.note: NEEDS INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION before being treated as confirmed.
